Every tighten gain is under 1.4 se, i.e. indistinguishable from hold on mean; their real effect is the tail (worst -1.18 -> -0.06, p05 -1.13 -> +0.18..+0.55), which is the only thing a lock-in buys. Why not take it: atr:1.0/1.5 put the stop 0.09R/0.34R from price (0.1-0.6 ATR, inside the 1 ATR min buffer, would be refused); atr:2.0 (+0.22R, ~0.1802) sits 1.06 ATR away but inside the last 6 hourly bars' noise (highs 0.1806-0.1813; the 17:00 bar ranged 0.0023), so a noise stop-out on a trending-down 4h is likelier than the table's SL-first replay shows, and that replay is biased in tighten's favour; r:0/0.41 are 0.8R/0.4R of room, same story. The class evidence (981 stop-tightens -0.097R) leans the same way but is not what decides it. Not defaulting to close-on-adverse and not tilting to hold: the arms were priced and none beats hold by a margin the table can see. Hold keeps the +3R target and the full tail: stop 0.18257 is 1.81R from open (-1R at entry), which is the exposure I accept; the 12-short crypto-beta book (ETH x3, SOL x2, AVAX x2, XRP, BTC) is one correlated bet, flagged. If the 1h closes back above 0.1807 with the 4h swing low 0.1775 unbroken, lock-in becomes the better call. The -0.13R/decision 14d figure is a whole-48-symbol replay, not this leg's live record; not weighed.
